trajectory_summary: This call moves in a straight, low-friction line from intro through verify to a booked appointment in about 14 minutes, with the customer cooperative throughout and volunteering useful detail (usage increase, EV plans, financial strain) largely unprompted. The rep completes the script mechanically and gets the sit, but leaves several forward-pulling anchors — the bill increase, the financial strain comment, the EV charger question, the co-owner mother — unused as leverage or follow-up.

observed_outcome.quote: Well, thanks so much for your time, Stacy. I got you down for tomorrow, the fifteenth, at 10AM.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day and time (tomorrow, the 15th, at 10AM) was confirmed for an in-person specialist visit ('we'll just have a local specialist drop by'), but the co-owner mother, Gail, was never invited or confirmed for the appointment.

bill_anchor_audit.bill_quote: my kilowatt hours is two eighty seven. And last year, it was one ninety five.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The customer surfaced both a dollar figure earlier (04:20, ~$129/$250 in winter) and a specific 47% usage-increase figure at 08:00, but the rep's responses ('Oh, really?' / 'So it's definitely gone up a little bit?') never turned either number into an explicit reason to act — the flip line that should have gone here never came.

bill_document_audit.ask_quote: The way that we design these systems is based on how much energy your home uses. And so we get everything we need off of your recent bill from Excel.
bill_document_audit.result_quote: It says this year as of March 2026, my kilowatt hours is two eighty seven. And last year, it was one ninety five.
bill_document_audit.reasoning: The rep asked for the bill's kWh graph and the customer pulled up their online Xcel account and read the numbers aloud live on the call, then the rep also arranged to email for a formal copy at 10:51-11:02.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep asked what got the customer interested in solar and got a clear bill-pain answer, but never explicitly tied the later usage-increase data or the appointment booking back to this stated motivation — it was captured but not reinforced.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: my kilowatt hours is two eighty seven. And last year, it was one ninety five.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer handed the rep the single strongest urgency lever on the call — a self-reported 47% usage increase — and the rep logged it for the design without reflecting it back as a reason to act now. This is the highest-leverage, most avoidable miss in an otherwise smooth call.

key_moments.quote: It says this year as of March 2026, my kilowatt hours is two eighty seven. And last year, it was one ninety five.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer hands over a striking data point — usage up 47% year over year — entirely unprompted, and the rep's only response is a flat acknowledgment before moving to the next data point. This was the single clearest bill-anchor opportunity on the call and it was filed, not flipped.

key_moments.quote: Yes. My mother is on the title with me. Her name is Gail Braemer.
key_moments.stewart_read: A co-owner was identified by name, which is the same structural trigger as the spouse_decision protocol — the person on title should be included in the appointment. The rep never revisits whether Gail should be on the closer call.

key_moments.quote: I think the city of Denver offers some financial assistance to get solar panels, so I'm considering that as well.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer discloses they are actively weighing a municipal assistance program as an alternative path — competitive context the closer would benefit from knowing. The rep does not probe (what program, has she applied, timeline) and moves straight into the address confirmation.

key_moments.quote: if I did qualify and I get solar panels and there's a certain number, right, that you put on the house, like, would I need to get more added if I get a charger added?
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer owns an EV bought in September and is actively planning a future charger/garage addition — a concrete future-load signal that increases the value of a rightsized or expandable system. The rep handled the redirect correctly by deferring to the specialist, but did not reflect the signal back as a reason to get excited about the appointment.
